title: Everything I Learned Training Frontier Small Models — Maxime Labonne, Liquid AI
talk_summary: Maxime Labonne (Liquid AI) explains how small edge models differ from scaled-down big models: they are memory-bound, narrow, latency-sensitive, and prone to doom loops on hard tasks. He details fixes: on-policy preference data with an LLM jury to reject degenerate rollouts, RLVR with n-gram repetition penalties, and offloading knowledge/long-context weaknesses to tools like web search and Python.

takeaways.technique: LLM-jury scoring of multiple rollouts to reject degenerate outputs
takeaways.what_they_do: Generate 5 temperature-sampled rollouts plus one greedy rollout per prompt, score all with an LLM jury, use best as chosen and worst as rejected for preference training; degenerate (doom-loop) outputs get rejected.
takeaways.evidence_quote: we give everything to a LLM jury to score all the um rollouts. We pick the best one
takeaways.numbers: 1M prompts; 5 sampled rollouts + 1 greedy; doom-loop ratio ~15-16% after pretraining, near zero after RL

takeaways.technique: Doom-loop / repetition ratio as a tracked metric
takeaways.what_they_do: Measure the fraction of generations that repeat sequences across many benchmarks as a first-class metric, tracked across training stages.
takeaways.evidence_quote: the doom loop ratio that we calculated across like a lot of benchmarks was about 15%
takeaways.numbers: ~15-16% after pretraining; barely moves after SFT; large drop after DPO; near zero after RL

takeaways.technique: Narrow task specialization over general capability
takeaways.what_they_do: Deliberately optimize small models for a few capabilities (data extraction, tool use) and accept being mediocre elsewhere, because users don't use them that way.
takeaways.evidence_quote: it's really nice to try to target some capabilities and not try to be like average on everything

takeaways.technique: Offload knowledge and long-context limits to tools
takeaways.what_they_do: Compensate for small-model knowledge gaps with web search tools and for long-context limits with a recursive Python environment that takes shortcuts.
takeaways.evidence_quote: if you have a tiny model, but it's able to Google everything ... you're going to have like much much better performance

takeaways.technique: Cold-start SFT data as diagnosis for failing tasks
takeaways.what_they_do: When RL on a task fails to train, they trace it back to missing similar examples in the supervised fine-tuning mixture and add them before retrying.
takeaways.evidence_quote: It's probably because you are missing some uh cold start SFT data

takeaways.technique: Verifiable-reward checks plus repetition penalty on agent loops
takeaways.what_they_do: Use RLVR where the final answer must be extractable to earn reward, and add an n-gram repetition penalty so looping trajectories are penalized.
takeaways.evidence_quote: you can add a bit of repetition penalty to make sure that um you are going to generate more like less doom loops
